title: Elevator controller and scheduling
idea: The core design is one ElevatorController that accepts calls, asks a SchedulingStrategy which car should answer, and lets each Elevator serve its stops with the LOOK algorithm.

analogy.text: A taxi dispatcher. A call comes in, the dispatcher picks a cab by a rule, and that cab adds the pickup to its route.
analogy.breaks: A cab drives anywhere; an elevator only goes up or down.

points: ElevatorController is a facade: callers see `hallCall`, `carCall` and `tick`.
SchedulingStrategy is the strategy pattern: each dispatch rule is a class.
NearestCarStrategy charges extra when a car must turn around first.
Each Elevator uses LOOK: keep direction while stops lie ahead, then reverse.

hero.title: One hall call through the design

steps.caption: Someone on floor 6 presses DOWN. The panel sends a hall call.
The controller does not pick a car itself. It asks the strategy.
The strategy scores each car in service. E2 at floor 8 costs 2; E1 at floor 0 costs 6.
The strategy returns E2. The controller adds floor 6 to E2's stops.
Each `tick` moves E2 one floor. LOOK keeps it going down while stops lie below.
At floor 6 the stop is removed and the doors open.
The hall call is served. The controller never knew how cars were scored.

code.title: Controller, strategy, LOOK
code.caption: The core flow in one file. Time is a tick counter, so every run prints the same trace.

walk.text: Two cars at floors 0 and 8, wired with NearestCarStrategy.
Two hall calls and one car call, then eight ticks of time.
A hall call asks the strategy for a car, then adds the stop.
Cost is distance when idle or passing; otherwise the trip via the farthest stop.
Each tick: close open doors, open at a stop, or move one floor.
LOOK keeps the current direction while stops remain ahead, then reverses.

code.title: A new strategy
code.caption: Zoning wraps any strategy as a new class. The copies below are trimmed: all cars are idle, so distance is the cost.

walk.text: Three cars. Zoning sends E1 and E2 to low floors, E3 to high floors.
Compare both strategies on the same calls, then with E1 out of service.
ZonedStrategy is a decorator: it filters cars by zone, then delegates to the inner strategy.
A Zone serves its range plus floor 0, the lobby every car shares.
The inner strategy skips cars that are out of service and breaks ties by id.

pitfalls: Do not add `if (peakHour)` branches to the controller; add a strategy class.
Never pick a car by distance alone; a car heading away is not close.
Skip OUT_OF_SERVICE cars inside the strategy, or calls go to a dead car.

quiz.q: What does ZonedDispatch print for floor 8 DOWN before E1 fails?
quiz.why: E3 at 12 is four floors away, so nearest picks it. Zoning drops E3 for floor 8; E1 and E2 tie, and the id picks E1.

takeaway: One facade controller; every dispatch rule is an injected strategy.

starters: How is LOOK different from SCAN for elevators?
Should a hall call ever be reassigned to a better car later?
How would I add a peak-hour strategy that parks cars at the lobby?
